description: Deterministic conservatism policy for ei-scope-resolver. The model proposes candidates; these rules decide what survives and what the resolver status may be. Rules only ever narrow a scope or lower a status.

rules.question: A proposed path, module or test cited no evidence, or cited an evidence id that does not exist. It was removed from the scope. Re-run the resolver with evidence, or confirm it is genuinely out of scope.
A proposed path falls inside a declared protected area and was removed. Confirm the protected area, or justify why it must change.
A proposed path or module belongs to a dependency that is still unresolved. Scope may not silently grow to cover it. Resolve the dependency first.
No defensible file survived the policy checks, so there is no scope to propose. Re-run the resolver with better evidence.
No domain context was supplied, so the owning implementation area could not be confirmed. Supply vocabulary/domain context and re-run.
The domain context reported ambiguous terms, so more than one implementation area may own this behaviour. A human must choose the area.
The proposed scope exceeds the defensible-size limits. Split the story or justify the breadth.
The story depends on something outside the apparent scope. The dependency is recorded, not included. A human must decide how it is handled.
A proposed path could not be verified against the repository. Confirm the path exists, or that the file is genuinely new.
Resolver confidence is below the minimum. Treat the proposal as a starting point for a human, not a conclusion.
No related tests were proposed. Identify the tests that prove the change, or state why none exist.
